name: GoleSync
tagline: Your Android phone and Linux laptop, talking over your own network.
summary: Connects an Android phone and a Linux laptop over the local network: clipboard, files, remote control and safe command buttons.
problem: Moving a link, a snippet or a file between a phone and a laptop usually means a cloud account or a cable. GoleSync does it directly over the local network, and keeps the laptop side locked down.

features.title: Text and clipboard
features.text: Push text and clipboard contents in both directions.

features.title: File drop
features.text: Send files between the phone and the laptop.

features.title: Phone as remote
features.text: Use the phone for slides, media, trackpad and keyboard.

features.title: Command buttons
features.text: Buttons on the phone run commands on the laptop, but only commands from an allow-list kept on the laptop.

howItWorks.text: The laptop runs a small FastAPI agent (X11). The phone pairs with it by scanning a QR code, and every request after that carries a token. Traffic stays on the local network, and commands only run if they appear on the laptop's allow-list.

thanks.text: Claude and Claude Code helped plan and write the app; I tested it on a real phone and laptop and decided what shipped.
